sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[db.Begin] --> C[borrow connection]
    C --> O1[tx.Exec op1] --> O2[tx.Exec op2]
    O2 --> OK{all succeeded?}
    OK -->|yes| CMT[tx.Commit — atomic]
    OK -->|any fail| RB[tx.Rollback — all undone]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The connection binding, the mechanism interviewers probe: a tx holds ONE connection from the pool for its entire life — the transaction's operations MUST go through tx (not db — db might route to a different connection, silently escaping the transaction). The classic bug: calling db.Exec inside a transaction block — the operation runs on a different connection, outside the transaction, not rolled back.

The context form (the modern discipline): tx, err := db.BeginTx(ctx, nil) — the context cancels, the transaction aborts. Request-scoped transactions: the handler's context carries through Begin, all Execs, and Commit — a client disconnect mid-transaction rolls it back, saving the DB from orphaned work.

The IsolationLevel tuning: the options parameter of BeginTx sets the level (sql.LevelSerializable for the strongest isolation, at concurrency cost). The default (each driver's default, usually read-committed) is right for most services; the higher levels are the banking/inventory trade.
